text: {"question":"How does the later 2026 measurement of the Hubble constant differ from the earlier 2025 baseline result, and what is the magnitude of that change?","reference_answer":"The 2026 analysis finds H0 = 67.24 ± 0.35 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, which is lower than the 2025 baseline value by about 1.1 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹—roughly a 1.6 % decrease, well within the quoted uncertainties.","passage_1_contribution":"The 2025 baseline reports the most accurate direct H0 measurement to date with a relative uncertainty of 1.09 % and agreement within 1σ with previous SH0ES determinations.","passage_2_contribution":"The 2026 study presents a revised H0 value of 67.24 ± 0.35 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, derived from updated Pantheon+ data and DES-DOVEKIE checks.","joint_reason":"Both passages report H0 values derived from distance‑scale measurements, allowing a direct comparison of the updated value to the earlier baseline.","same_quantity":true}
